sections.title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
sections.abstract: The author says this short note exposits a recent proof of the Kozma–Nitzan conjecture attributed to OpenAI.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract reports an exposition of the recent proof; it does not state the theorem or proof details, so the result is reported only as the author characterizes it.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A probability-theory conjecture; the abstract does not specify the conjecture’s hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an exposition of a claimed proof, not independent proof verification; the abstract alone is insufficient to assess the argument or its exact scope.
sections.ranking_evidence: Targeted search surfaced an October MathDB entry about the claimed proof exposition and earlier discussion by mathematician Gil Kalai; this is topic-level attention, not verification of this note.

sections.title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
sections.abstract: Using Hodge–Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, the authors prove a weighted inequality for flats and apply it to the points–lines–planes conjecture and Brylawski’s ultra-log-concavity conjecture, including equality cases.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive the points–lines–planes inequality and Brylawski’s ultra-log-concavity of first-kind Whitney numbers from a weighted inequality for rank-graded flats, with equality characterizations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite loopless matroids; the weighted theorem assigns real weights to flats of a fixed intermediate rank.
sections.unique_caveat: These are preprint claims; the report checked the introduction and stated main theorem, not the proofs.
sections.ranking_evidence: The claimed results resolve two specifically named conjectures and characterize equality in both; an independent commentary page discusses the result but is not a peer-review signal.

sections.title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
sections.abstract: For even vertex counts, the authors prove that a random 3-uniform hypergraph process gets a loose Hamilton cycle exactly when its last isolated vertex disappears, with high probability, and report extensions to other fixed uniformities and counting estimates.
sections.claimed_result: For even n, the first loose Hamilton cycle in the 3-uniform process appears with high probability when the final isolated vertex disappears; extensions are reported for fixed r≥4 with (r−1)|n, with cycle counts estimated within exp{o(n)}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Uniformly add missing edges to an initially empty hypergraph; the main 3-uniform result is asymptotic through even n.
sections.unique_caveat: The main theorem is asymptotic and has a parity restriction; the reported counting estimate is only within a subexponential factor, not a sharp asymptotic equivalent.
sections.ranking_evidence: The introduction identifies the hitting-time question as posed in earlier literature; the paper links a Lean 4 formalization and describes extensions to fixed higher uniformities and cycle counts.

sections.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
sections.abstract: For univariate Gaussian location mixtures, the authors establish minimax squared-Hellinger risk rates for unconstrained and compact-support-constrained nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimators, using local bracketing-entropy bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The unconstrained NPMLE attains squared-Hellinger rate log(n)/n for sub-Gaussian mixing; for compactly supported mixing with a matching compact constraint the rate is log(n)/(n log log n).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Univariate location mixtures with known standard Gaussian kernel; sub-Gaussian mixing for the unconstrained result, and compact support for the faster constrained result.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantees concern density estimation in this specific mixture model; they do not establish the same rates for multivariate mixtures, unknown component variance, or arbitrary mixing tails.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in statistics, information theory, and machine learning; states two minimax-optimal rates and a local entropy technique. The introduction and main results were inspected.

sections.title: A Sharp Bound for Additive Complements
sections.abstract: For infinite nonnegative-integer sets whose sum contains all sufficiently large integers, the author proves a sharp implication from a limsup bound on the product of their counting functions.
sections.claimed_result: If A+B contains every sufficiently large integer and limsup A(x)B(x)/x < 3/2, then A(x)B(x)−x tends to positive infinity; the author says 3/2 is best possible.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A and B are infinite subsets of nonnegative integers, A(x), B(x) are their counting functions, and their sumset is cofinite.
sections.unique_caveat: The implication assumes a strict limsup bound below 3/2; it does not settle the boundary case at equality.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract states an explicit sharp constant and a discrete gap argument; no separate attention signal was found in sources checked.

sections.title: On ABP Estimates for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations and Applications
sections.abstract: The authors establish a weighted Alexandrov–Bakelman–Pucci estimate for fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and gradient dependence, then apply it to several nonlinear PDE classes.
sections.claimed_result: A weighted ABP-type bound is established for classical subsolutions and viscosity subsolutions with locally Lipschitz gradients, allowing general gradient-growth rates subject to a smallness condition when the associated weight has finite integral.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and nonlinear gradient dependence; Hessian-quotient applications require an additional condition on the contact Hessian.
sections.unique_caveat: Applicability depends on stated regularity, gradient-weight, and data-smallness conditions; the Hessian-quotient application has an extra contact-Hessian hypothesis.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract lists applications to generalized Monge–Ampère, Hessian, Hessian-quotient, and anisotropic mean-curvature-type equations; broad PDE relevance is an isolated signal in this selection.
